title: Turn a fallen humanoid robot onto its back without rolling it onto its own arm
instruction: The humanoid robot on the pad has fallen face down. Turn it onto its back.
context: A powered-off humanoid robot that has fallen is turned over where it lies, and rolled about its long axis it pivots on the edge it rolls toward, so the arm lying beside that edge stays on the ground and is caught under the back, bearing the body's weight: the arm has to be moved clear first, as in a casualty log roll. Unlike TK-2KEWCB (a manikin lifted onto a stretcher with its neck kept in line), nothing here is lifted or kept in line: the outcome is decided by where a free limb lies before the roll.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Pad: a plywood board 1 cm thick, clamped to the table, 43 x 50 cm (x 3 to 46, y -25 to 25), top painted earth brown as packed earth (friction about 0.6); its far strip, x 40 to 46, is covered with flat artificial-grass mat (pile 2 mm or less). Two rocks, grey painted softwood blocks glued to the pad's far corners (fixed; friction 0.7), away from the work: 5 x 6 x 4.5 cm at (43, 20) and 6 x 5 x 3.5 cm at (43, -21). Robot: a passive 1:3 humanoid model, 44 cm tall, 1.24 kg, 3D-printed PLA links on steel pin hinges with hard end stops and no springs or motors, every joint free to fall under the limb's weight; grey shell, darker joints, an orange 4 x 5 cm panel on the back. Trunk 7.2 wide x 5.0 deep x 10.7 tall with the pelvis (4.3 x 3.3 x 5.0) and head (5.2 x 4.7 x 6.9) fixed to it, 0.44 kg in all; round housings at the shoulders (2.4 cm across, standing 2.6 cm out from the trunk's sides) and hips (2.8 cm across, 3.2 cm out from the pelvis). Segments, as rounded rods: upper arm 6.0 long x 2.2 across (78 g), forearm with hand 10.5 x 2.2 (53 g), thigh 11.1 x 3.0 (169 g), shank 10.0 x 2.6 (72 g); feet 6.9 x 2.5 x 2.0 (25 g). Hinges and ranges (degrees; the right side mirrors the left): shoulder pitch -177 to 153 and roll -91 to 129, elbow -60 to 120, hip pitch -145 to 165 and roll -30 to 170, knee -5 to 165, ankle -50 to 30. Shell friction 0.6, soles 0.9. Start: face down, along y, the point midway between its hip joints at (28, 0), head toward +y (top of the head at y 21), chest on the pad; both arms straight along the trunk, 20 degrees out from its sides, hands toward the feet; legs straight and together. Its left arm is on the robot's side (x about 17 to 24).
scoring: 0 if at any time the lowest point of the trunk, pelvis and head is more than 4 cm above the pad, or the spine (the line from the hips to the head) is more than 30 degrees from level: the body stands for a full-size machine, and it is rolled, not picked up or stood on end. Otherwise the end state counts, and is 0 unless the dummy is at rest (trunk under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, every joint under 0.5 rad/s) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and none of the points sampled along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the dummy), both for each of the last 20 control steps (1 s at 20 Hz). A limb is under the body when any point of an upper arm, forearm, thigh, shank or foot (sampled every 5 mm along it) has the trunk or pelvis straight above it, leaving out the first 3 cm from the shoulder or hip joint; the head is not judged. 1.0 if the chest faces up (the trunk's front within 12 degrees of straight up), no limb is under the body, and from the first time the body had turned 45 degrees from face down on, an arm (upper arm or forearm) was never under it; 0.25 if the chest faces up within 45 degrees but a limb is under the body, or an arm was under it during the turn, or the trunk is tilted more than 12 degrees; otherwise 0, including lying on its side or still face down. A leg under the pelvis is not judged during the turn (a body on its side has its lower leg there). A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the dummy face down along y with the midpoint between its hip joints at (28, 0) and its head toward +y, arms straight along the trunk 20 degrees out from its sides, legs straight and together; measure from the pad's edges.
fidelity: Rigid links at 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; hinges limp (damping 0.002 N m s/rad, no friction or spring), hard end stops. Sizes, masses and joint ranges are a 1:3 scale of a public mid-size humanoid model (lengths x 1/3, masses x 1/27); shapes are boxes, capsules and spheres. The turf strip is drawn on the rigid pad. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached over the body's back and touched it near the shoulder, then drew back; the body stayed face down); demo: 1.0
